rationale: The same feeding told in the same order and much of the same wording in the BSB: "I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat" (Matthew 15:32; Mark 8:2), "Where in this desolate place" (15:33; 8:4), "How many loaves do you have?" and "Seven" (15:34; 8:5), the crowd told "to sit down on the ground" (15:35; 8:6), "seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over" (15:37; 8:8), and a boat trip afterward. The basket word is spyris in both, as against kophinos at the five thousand; lesson 30 already notes that difference. Parallel/strong rather than explicit, following conn-matt14-feeding-mark6. The differences are real: Matthew has "a few small fish" in the disciples' answer and one thanksgiving over loaves and fish together (15:34, 15:36), where Mark has the fish appear later with their own blessing (8:7); only Matthew adds "in addition to women and children" (15:38); Mark says "some of them have come a great distance" (8:3); and the landing place is "Magadan" in Matthew and "Dalmanutha" in Mark, which Augustine (Harmony 2.51) and Calvin take as one district under two names. Whether this feeding is a second event or a second telling of the first is reported in the lesson's Positions, not decided by this row.
